_comment: Catalogue for the examples dropdown on the slicer page.
To add a circuit: drop a .py file in this directory and add an entry here.
A .py file with no entry still shows up, under 'Unsorted', using its filename.
Every entry's claims were checked against the analyser's actual output;
if you change a circuit, re-check its blurb.
A .qasm entry goes to the OpenQASM front end, which parses without executing.

examples.title: Bell pair
examples.blurb: One Hadamard and one CNOT: the smallest circuit that entangles two qubits.
examples.highlight: Try: slice backward from either measurement -- you get both gates.

examples.title: Two independent wires
examples.blurb: No two-qubit gate, so nothing entangles. The control case for slicing.
examples.highlight: Try: slice backward from #3 -- 2 instructions, not 4.

examples.title: GHZ state
examples.blurb: A chain of CNOTs spreads one entangled group across three qubits.
examples.highlight: Try: watch the group absorb a qubit at each CNOT.

examples.title: Phase kickback
examples.blurb: A controlled gate that changes the control instead of the target -- the mechanism every oracle below runs on.

examples.title: Swap test
examples.blurb: Measures the overlap between two states using a controlled swap.
examples.highlight: Try: a three-qubit gate drawn as one node across three wires.

examples.title: Grover search (2 qubits)
examples.blurb: Oracle plus diffuser, marking |11>. Small enough to read every edge in the graph.
examples.highlight: Try: slice backward from #12 -- 11 of 14 instructions.

examples.title: Deutsch-Jozsa
examples.blurb: Decides constant versus balanced in a single oracle query.

examples.title: Bernstein-Vazirani
examples.blurb: Recovers a hidden bit string in one query. Only the wires whose bit is 1 are touched.
examples.highlight: Try: compare the slice from #15 (untouched wire) with #16.

examples.title: Simon's algorithm
examples.blurb: Finds the hidden period of a 2-to-1 function. Two registers bridged only by the oracle.

examples.title: QFT (written out)
examples.blurb: Three-qubit Fourier transform, every controlled rotation spelled out as its own node.
examples.highlight: Try: note how nearly everything depends on everything.

examples.title: QFT (from qiskit.circuit.library)
examples.blurb: The same transform pulled from the Qiskit library instead of hand-written.
examples.highlight: Try: compare the gate names with the hand-written version.

examples.title: Phase estimation
examples.blurb: Reads the eigenphase of the T gate into three counting qubits.

examples.title: QAOA MaxCut (one layer)
examples.blurb: Cost and mixer layers over a four-node ring. Every rzz is both entangling and phase-carrying.

examples.title: Variational ansatz
examples.blurb: Two layers of rotations and entanglers, the shape most VQE circuits take.

examples.title: Quantum teleportation
examples.blurb: Mid-circuit measurement and classical feed-forward. The clearest measurement dependency in the set.
examples.highlight: Try: keep only Measurement edges, then slice backward from the first correction.

examples.title: Superdense coding
examples.blurb: Two classical bits carried by one qubit, using a Bell pair agreed in advance.
examples.highlight: Try: slice from q1's measurement -- it reaches the encoding gates on q0.

examples.title: Entanglement swapping
examples.blurb: Entangles two qubits that no gate ever touched together.
examples.highlight: Try: slice from #11 with all edges, then with Data Qubit only.

examples.title: Uncomputation (detected)
examples.blurb: An adjacent pair of identical single-qubit gates, which the analyser does record as uncomputation.
examples.highlight: Try: instruction #3 under 'uncomputed' in the Entanglement tab.

examples.title: Ancilla uncompute (missed)
examples.blurb: The same idea with Toffolis, which the analyser does not catch yet -- a known gap, not a bug in the circuit.
examples.highlight: Try: compare its groups with uncomputation.py.

examples.title: Bit-flip code
examples.blurb: Encode, inject an error, extract a syndrome, correct. The longest measurement-dependency chain here.

examples.title: Static-check showcase
examples.blurb: Runs fine, but trips three checks: no measurement, an idle qubit, and a cancelling gate pair.
examples.highlight: Try: read the Diagnostics panel rather than the graph.

examples.title: Large circuit (viewer stress test)
examples.blurb: Six qubits, 44 instructions, 58 edges. Exists to make the graph awkward.
examples.highlight: Try: the Range control, then pan and zoom.

examples.title: GHZ state (OpenQASM)
examples.blurb: The same GHZ circuit as an OpenQASM 3 file. This route parses the text and runs nothing.
examples.highlight: Try: compare the graph with the Python version -- it is identical.

examples.title: Grover search (OpenQASM)
examples.blurb: Exported with qiskit.qasm3.dumps(). Gate names are whatever the export chose, not what the source said.
examples.highlight: Try: note that the static checks are skipped -- they only read Python.
